name: Lepus
introduction: is the Hare, crouching at the feet of Orion and chased by his dogs. Its stars form a compact shape just south of Orion, best seen on northern winter evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Lepus contains one of the reddest stars in the sky: R Leporis, Hind’s Crimson Star, a carbon star whose atmosphere is so rich in carbon soot that it glows a deep blood red. It slowly varies in brightness over about 14 months.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Arneb](hip:25985), the brightest star, is a yellow-white supergiant more than 2,000 light-years away, thousands of times more luminous than the Sun. [Nihal](hip:25606) is a yellow bright giant.
[Gamma Leporis](hip:27072), only 29 light-years away, is a Sun-like star with a wide companion. [Mu Leporis](hip:24305) has an unusual surface rich in mercury and manganese.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The globular cluster M79 may not have formed in the Milky Way at all; it may have come from a dwarf galaxy that our galaxy has absorbed.
